gate: 14.1 — AgentCore Runtime capability-fit and authority boundary

observations: AgentCore Runtime supports HTTP, MCP, A2A, and AG-UI protocols.
HTTP uses /invocations; MCP uses /mcp; A2A and AG-UI are separate service contracts.
Supported inbound authentication includes SigV4 and OAuth 2.0.
Runtime session identifiers provide microVM stickiness and isolation semantics.
Session identity does not replace application-owned user-to-session ownership.
Runtime execution-role temporary credentials are exposed inside the microVM through MMDS.
Least-privilege execution-role design is mandatory because code running inside the VM can attempt to use those credentials.
Direct code deployment is intended for rapid iteration with ZIP artifacts.
Direct code deployment has a 250 MB compressed and 750 MB uncompressed package limit.
Container deployment remains available when packaging or native dependency requirements justify it.
Runtime CPU and memory are billed from actual consumption rather than a fixed monthly allocation.
Published runtime list prices observed on the decision date are USD 0.0895 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.00945 per GB-hour.
OpsLens runtime cost remains unmeasured until an authenticated bounded replay exists.
The resource supports direct-code or container artifacts, PUBLIC or VPC network modes, lifecycle settings, HTTP/MCP/A2A/AGUI protocol selection, and optional custom JWT authorizer configuration.

retained_opslens_boundaries: MCP is an interoperability boundary, not new business authority.
Phase 11 bounded single-agent reasoning remains the retained measured reasoning reference.
Phase 12 deterministic specialization/handoff remains retained; the measured two-model topology is not the default.
Phase 13 bounded offline MCP architecture remains retained and is not automatically promoted into a deployed runtime.

decision.first_hosted_boundary: retained Phase 11 bounded single-agent reasoning path
decision.first_experiment_stop_boundary: deterministic authorization outcome before capability execution

explicit_non_claims: runtime exposure or Amazon Inspector evidence
